https://hungarytoday.hu/chinese-investor.text: Chinese Investors Working to Find Common Language with New Government At a press briefing, Chinese Ambassador to Hungary Mr. Gong Tao highlighted the expanding scope of China-Hungary relations. Speaking about Chinese investment in Hungary, he also addressed the challenges companies can encounter in complying with Hungarian and EU environmental regulations. Ambassador Mr. Gong Tao mentioned that he had recently met and held discussions with several ministers of the new Hungarian government. He also noted that the CATL battery factory in Debrecen had received an operating license from the Hungarian authorities, paving the way for the start of battery-cell production. CATL factory. Photo: Facebook /Joó István Fact CATL recently came under scrutiny from the TISZA government after green liquid was discharged into the sewer system at its Debrecen plant in violation of regulations. While authorities took action over the incident and revoked the plant’s industrial wastewater pre-treatment permit, CATL said the substance was a non-toxic leak-detection dye that posed no risk to people or the environment. Government testing also found no harmful contamination, although the company acknowledged that the discharge itself violated regulations. In recent years, China has become one of the largest foreign investors in Hungary and Chinese investment is set to continue. At the same time, the embassy understands the need for companies to strictly comply with Hungarian laws and applicable EU environmental regulations. In this regard, the topic of Semcorp has also been mentioned, a Chinese battery-component manufacturer operating in Debrecen whose production was suspended by Hungarian authorities in June over suspected environmental pollution. Semcorp. Photo: MTI /Derencsényi István According to the ambassador, the company cooperated with the authorities, commissioned additional testing by qualified laboratories, and sought assessments from environmental experts. Semcorp later said the new tests found no evidence that the factory had caused the pollution cited in the shutdown order, and that the relevant reports had been submitted to the Hungarian authorities. Beyond investment and environmental issues, the ambassador also emphasized that Chinese-Hungarian relations extend into a much broader range of areas, including tourism, culture, and education. In this regard, he noted that this year, 24 direct passenger flights per week have been operating between Hungary and seven major Chinese cities, bringing 130,000 Chinese tourists to the country. https://www.zerohedge.com/geopolitical/a.text: ZeroHedge Reads Alt-Market AntiWar.com Bitcoin Magazine Bombthrower BULLIONSTAR Capitalist Exploits Christophe Barraud Dollar Collapse Dr. Housing Bubble Financial Revolutionist ForexLive Forum Geopolitica Gains Pains & Capital Gefira GMG Research Gold Core Implode-Explode Insider Paper Libertarian Institute Liberty Blitzkrieg Max Keiser Mises Institute Mish Talk Monetary Metals Newsquawk Of Two Minds Oil Price Open The Books Peter Schiff Portfolio Armor QTR’s Fringe Finance Safehaven Slope of Hope SpotGamma TF Metals Report The Automatic Earth The Burning Platform The Economic Populist Themis Trading Thoughtful Money Value Walk Visual Combat Banzai7 Wolf Street Expand Authored by Andrew Korybko via Substack , The potential pullback of some US forces from the Baltic States upon the completion of its force posture review could be followed by European NATO if Russia agrees to pull back some of its forces from Belarus in order to then establish partial buffers in the post-war European security architecture. NBC reported last week that the US is considering withdrawing up to half of its ~80,000 troops that are deployed to Europe along with large amounts of equipment. This coincides with European fearmongering led by Poland and France that Russia plans to ramp up its hybrid attacks against European NATO (E-NATO) into increasingly regular kinetic ones that it'll then deny. E-NATO is also undergoing rapid militarization led by Poland and Germany while deploying ever more forces to Russia's doorstep . These sky-high NATO-Russian tensions might be reduced upon the US' potential drawdown of its forces in Europe depending on the success of the following creative diplomatic proposal. If some US forces are pulled from the Baltic States, then the US might coerce its E-NATO allies to follow suit if Russia does the same with at least some of its forces in Belarus, which they fear could be exploited by it as a launchpad into the Baltic States. The military-strategic logic behind this proposal requires some explanation. Just as E-NATO fears that Russia could exploit Belarus as a launchpad into the Baltic States, so too does Russia fear that E-NATO could exploit the Baltic States as a launchpad into either Kaliningrad, Belarus, or "mainland Russia". E-NATO claims that its gradual military build-up in the Baltic States is to deter Russia while Russia's own regional build-up is arguably to deter E-NATO. The resultant security dilemma risks a major war by miscalculation or a (Ukrainian?) false flag and is why tensions must urgently be reduced. The key to this proposal is Belarus, Russia's mutual defense and Union State ally with which the US is in the midst of a fast-moving rapprochement marked by phased sanctions relief in exchange for the release of so-called "political prisoners". President Alexander Lukashenko is receptive to Trump 2.0's outreaches in order to reduce multifaceted Western pressure on Belarus since the large-scale phase of the Ukrainian Conflict began nearly half a decade ago and to counterbalance disproportionate dependence on Russia. They and Putin could thus agree to an arrangement whereby any planned American military drawdown from the Baltic States leads to a partial drawdown of Russian forces in Belarus, incentivized by more sanctions relief for both of them, conditional on E-NATO pulling back its forces from the Baltic States. Poland, where Trump is considering a permanent US military presence and which already commands E-NATO's largest army , could then become the bloc's military bastion if they redeploy their forces to there. It was earlier explained why " Poland Would Be The Baltic States' Best Security Guarantor In NATO 3.0 ", namely due to geographic reasons, the aforesaid military factors, and its envisaged leadership of the Intermarium . If this arrangement is implemented, then it could turn the Baltic States and Belarus into partial buffers, both of which would remain under their allies' mutual defense umbrellas for deterrence purposes, which could spark progress on Ukraine's negotiated demilitarization for the same purpose. If coupled with a Russian-American(-Polish?) mechanism for verifying compliance and addressing issues as they may emerge (e.g. Ukrainian drone flights over Belarusian and Baltic airspace), then tensions could be reduced and a basis for the post-war European security architecture would be established. All eyes are therefore on Belarus ahead of the US' reported European military drawdown since that country and its leader are the key to this vision for averting a major war in the most realistic way possible. https://balkaninsight.com/2026/10/16/dem.text: Elsewhere, Slovakia to revive cooperation with Russia at meeting planned for November 25; Hungary parliament approves new child protection legislation; and Czech Army chief warns of possible Russian attack A 66-year-old Polish man was charged this week with plotting to assassinate PM Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Władyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz as part of an alleged plan to overthrow the government by force. The suspect was arrested in Wroclaw on Sunday after security services received a tip-off about a possible attack. “The man who threatened an assassination attempt has been detained,” Tusk wrote on X, thanking police for their “swift and decisive action”. Police searching the suspect’s home discovered more than a dozen improvised explosive devices resembling fragmentation grenades, alongside other weapons. Subsequently, prosecutors have brought nine charges, including preparing to overthrow constitutional authorities using explosives, inciting hate crimes and promoting Russia’s war against Ukraine, the most serious of which carries a maximum 15-year prison sentence. The suspect, reportedly active in far-right extremist circles, has denied the allegations and will be held in custody for two months, following a Wednesday court decision. The new law imposes stricter obligations on media outlets and political parties to protect minors’ rights. Media outlets must label content that may be harmful to under-18s, while political parties are no longer allowed to use billboards that incite fear or hatred in their political campaigns. Tighter restrictions on billboards – a campaign tool favoured by Fidesz during its 16 years in power – have long been a demand of the now-governing Tisza party, particularly following the most recent election campaign, when Fidesz accused Tisza – falsely – of planning to involve Hungary in the war in Ukraine and send young Hungarians to the battlefield. The new legislation removed the anti-LGBTQ+ provisions introduced by Fidesz in 2021, which the Court of Justice of the European Union also found incompatible with EU values. The previous wording explicitly prohibited the display and promotion of homosexual content to under-18s, a provision that led to controversial measures such as requiring certain children’s books to be wrapped in plastic. The revised legislation, instead, prohibits the promotion of all explicit sexual content, including pornography, sexual exploitation, abuse or age-inappropriate materials. However, it stops short of suspending the controversial government decree requiring books to be wrapped. “This is surely not one of the main concerns of Hungarian society,” PM Peter Magyar said in an interview with the YouTube channel Partizan when asked whether the wrapping would be upheld. Hungarian Foreign Minister Anita Orban and PM Magyar both welcomed the Ukrainian parliament’s adoption on Monday of a law expanding language rights for Hungarians and other national minorities in Ukraine. The law brings significant improvement for ethnic minorities whose language is an EU language, but does not apply to Russians. The legislation introduces a new category, the status of a “national minority general secondary education institution”, which applies to schools where more than half of the students are taught in a minority language. These institutions will enjoy greater autonomy in shaping their curricula. While Ukrainian literature and history will be taught in Ukrainian, most other subjects may be taught in minority languages. Students will also be allowed to take university entrance examinations in their mother tongue, and official documents and certificates will be issued in minority languages. Ukraine restricted the use of minority languages in education in 2017, sparking hostilities with Hungary over the rights of ethnic minorities. Former Hungarian PM Viktor Orban used the contested language law as grounds for blocking EU aid to Ukraine and vetoing the start of its EU membership talks. The Tisza government promised to mend ties with Ukraine, but also demanded radical improvement in language rights. After the law was adopted, the government swiftly lifted its veto to allow the opening of two more EU “clusters” (negotiating chapters) with Ukraine. “After years of inaction and frozen reactions, we have managed to ensure that the Transcarpathian Hungarian minority regained its rights,” Magyar told a press conference. The law was subsequently signed by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, which could pave the way for a bilateral meeting between the two leaders in the autumn.
